text:
kelsey: Need a concise "roadmap canvas" for routing segmentation that ties to launch gates, migration constraints, and a simple pricing story. Sales wants something demo-friendly; infra wants clear runbooks.

omar: Agreed. My recommendation: define four pragmatic lanes (shared-shard, geo-guard, quarantine-lane, tenant-island) and for each call out: latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), burst cap, KV policy, egress_allowed flag, and commercial prerequisite (if any). Keep it consumable.

nova: From customer calls: the two repeat asks are data residency and predictable tail latency. They will accept throughput limits for stronger isolation, but they want numbers up-front.

prashant: For engineering: include a minimal policy DSL (YAML-like) and a CI policy validator that fails merges when constraints are violated. Also list the mandatory chaos tests per lane (slow-link, partial-region-loss, cache-invalidation).

kelsey: Proposed v1 launch gates: 1) policy DSL + linter + unit tests, 2) per-tenant cost estimator + finance sign-off on multipliers, 3) telemetry dashboard tiles + alert playbook, 4) migration runbook with pilot tenants (3-7) and soft-eviction <2hr, 5) legal/regulatory checklist for quarantine-lane.

sales-bot: @marco requested a simple UI toggle copy and a one-line selling point per lane for demos. Also asked for a sample pricing band per lane by model class.

omar: Operational nuance: quarantine-lane defaults to no peeking. If peeking is enabled (opt-in) we must publish expected p99 delta and an estimated egress multiplier. Also require tenant acknowledgement of potential cold-starts if peeking is off.

prashant: Migration expectations: tenant-island requires Reserved Capacity contract before cutover. Rollback time objective: route back to the shared-shard or geo-guard compatible variant within 20 minutes. CI must include rollback drills.

nova: Sales UX idea: a three-state toggle: "Standard / Guarded / Dedicated" with short tooltips. Tooltip examples: Standard = cost-optimal, Guarded = residency + predictable p99, Dedicated = isolated compute + SLA. Also add a small help link to explain uplift ranges.

kelsey: We'll include a mapping table of "model family -> recommended default lane" so customers don't have to choose blindly (e.g., small-embed: shared-shard, high-throughput-chat: geo-guard, regulated-qa: quarantine-lane, heavy-LLM: tenant-island).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: policy-canvas v1 deployed to canary cluster canary-77 (link: https://ci.redwood/rollouts/canvas-v1-77). Logs available.

prashant: Add a small code snippet for the one-pager (YAML style) that the policy linter can parse. Keep fields minimal.

```
policy:
  lane: quarantine-lane
  affinity: hard-residency
  kv: region-local
  peeking: false
  burst_cap_tps: 100
  fallback: regional-compat-quant
  sla:
    p99_ms: 150
```

kelsey: For pricing, finance prefers ranges instead of fixed numbers initially. Example band guidance for demos: shared-shard (+0-15%), geo-guard (+15-45%), quarantine-lane (+40-90%), tenant-island (+100-300%) depending on model family and throughput. We'll annotate that these are starting points subject to final quoting.

nova: Also include an "eviction SLA" paragraph for customer docs: e.g., "During severe incidents, tenants on Guarded and Quarantine lanes may be soft-evicted for up to 2 hours while we remediate; Tenant-Island includes a separate operational SLA tied to Reserved Capacity."

omar: Testing: require chaos sims for any lane that allows peeking. Document the test matrix and expected tolerances. We should also run a simple microbenchmark to estimate p99 delta with peeking on vs off and include those numbers in the appendix.

prashant: CI/automation: policy PRs must pass the linter, unit tests, and a quick validator that estimates egress delta and flags high-cost peeking configs. We can gate PRs into main until we have the one-pager approved.

kelsey: Action items: kelsey -> draft the canvas one-pager (tier table, launch gates, minimal DSL, pricing bands) by EOD Friday; prashant -> author migration/rollback runbook + CI validator stub; omar -> run peeking vs local sims and provide p99 delta estimates; nova -> sales toggle copy and demo FAQ. Reconvene Monday 10am.

nova: One UX ask: keep the toggle wording customer-friendly and avoid technical jargon in the initial demo. Provide an "advanced details" modal for technical buyers that includes the YAML snippet and evacuation/playbook references.

kelsey: Agreed. v1 default = no peeking, region-local cache. Opt-in peeking must be explicit at activation time.

omar: I'll also prepare a short ops checklist for pilot migrations so SRE has a repeatable script.

prashant: Note for legal: quarantine-lane may require a signed data-processing addendum in some markets. Add that to the gate checklist.

kelsey: Thanks everyone. If we keep the canvas tight and the DSL intentionally tiny we can reduce rollout surprises and give sales something concrete to work with. Posting draft Friday.
